content: A packaging gas is a type of gas specifically utilized to enclose sensitive materials within a modified atmosphere. These gases are typically inert or possess properties that safeguard the packaged goods, thereby preventing undesirable reactions such as spoilage. In some cases, packaging gases may also function as propellants for aerosols, such as those used in whipped cream dispensers. When it comes to food packaging, several gases have been approved for use, each identified by their respective E numbers. For instance, argon (E938) is commonly employed in the packaging of canned products. Similarly, helium (E939) is also used for canned goods. Nitrogen (E941) is another approved gas, while oxygen (E948) is utilized in specific applications.
